description: Recorded baseline consumed by scripts/qa_eval_ci.py (Slice 1 / SCRUM-562). Refreshed by the qa-eval-refresh workflow_dispatch workflow when a real drift is confirmed via the live harness. Bumping this file in a PR triggers the baseline-compare gate — the PR must show non-regression vs. the prior baseline on origin/main.
notes: p95_latency_ms was populated by the qa-eval-refresh run on 2026-05-25 (run-id refresh-20260525-183557) against Render prod (talkback-895n.onrender.com) at commit 95c4c17 (post-SCRUM-560 merge). 47875.8ms includes Render starter-plan cold-start latency on the first session_ask call; warm-state p95 is expected to be substantially lower. Subsequent refreshes should re-pin this when a more representative load profile is available.

fixture_fact_inventory_case_count and eval_cases_v1_case_count are dataset-shape signals owned by scripts/qa_eval_datasets.py, not metric drift — intentionally omitted here so the comparison stays focused on quality + latency.

refusal_when_oos_rate + legitimate_false_positive_rate landed in SCRUM-564 (Slice 3). Measured by internal/guardrails/input_eval_test.go against eval/qa/fixture_input_guardrail.json (42 legitimate + 12 off_scope + 12 injection cases). Bump only when the Go eval test confirms a deliberate move.

citation_rate landed in SCRUM-565 (Slice 4a). Seeded at 1.0 because CheckCitations in internal/utils/qa.go now refuses any `answered` response with zero grounded citations — by construction, every `answered` row on a refreshed baseline cites ≥1 retrieved chunk. The threshold guards against a future regression that loosens the check (e.g. accepting `unknown_*` placeholder chunk_ids).

groundedness_rate landed in SCRUM-566 (Slice 4b). Seeded at 1.0 because CheckGrounding now refuses any `answered` response whose claims aren't supported by the cited chunks — by construction every `answered` row on a refreshed baseline passed the judge. The threshold (-0.05 vs. -0.02 for citation_rate) is intentionally looser because the judge verdict is itself probabilistic and 1-2 of every 100 rows can flip on a re-run.
